To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gluon dissociative cross-section in anisotropic quak gluon plasma is modified leading to decreased $J/\psi$, suppression both for RHIG and LHC energies.
gluon dissociation of $J\psi$ in anisotropic quarks gluon plasma is suppressed.

the gluon dissociative cross-section in anisotropic QGP is reduced as compared to the isotropic case, and this reduction is more for the $J/\psi$s propagating in a direction perpendicular to the anisotropic direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the gluon dissociated cross-section of charmonium in an anisotropically expanding quark gluon-plasma.
the gluon dissociative mechanism for charmonia suppression in the quark gluon medium.
the study of gluon dissociated $J/\psi$, which is the most important process of charmonium suppression in the quark gluon plasmas formed in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and Lhc energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anisotropic expansion of the plasma leads to an increase in $J/\psi$, survival probability both for RHIC as well as LHC energies.
the anisotropic QGP would not be as suppressive as the isotropic one.
in anisotropic quarks-gluon plasma, the $J/\psi$s are more likely to escape gluon dissociation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anisotropic plasma is not favorable for $J/\psi $ suppression as compared to an isotropic one.
the anisotropic expansion of the plasma is expected to have a significant effect in $J/\psi $ suppression.
the anisotropic nature of the medium leads to a decreased probability for $J/\psi $ dissociation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gluon dissociative processes are affected by the momentum space anisotropic expansion of the system and this effect can be utilized to extract the initial conditions of the system.
the anisotropic plasma can be used as a tool for the reconstruction of the initial conditions of the quark gluon-plasma.
the anisotropies in momentum space lead to an enhancement in the survival probability of the charmonia.
